**Rare Nirvana Photographs and Web Preservation Efforts**

In recent news, rare photographs from Nirvana's first concert in March 1987 have been unearthed and shared by Maggie Poukkula, the 19-year-old daughter of Tony Poukkula, a member of Seattle band Laytem who hosted the fledging outfit's first show in his basement. The photographs, which feature Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic, and Aaron Burckhard, showcase the band's early days and include covers of Led Zeppelin songs. Poukkula discovered the photos tucked away in her father's biographies of Cobain and Nirvana.

Meanwhile, the Internet Archive is working to preserve web pages and fix broken links. The organization's "No More 404" initiative aims to archive pages as they are created and reference the versions that were live when the page was written. This effort aims to preserve the original content and intent of web pages, even if the referenced pages are taken down or changed.

Additionally, the documentary "Montage of Heck," which features rare Cobain and Nirvana artifacts, is set to return to movie theaters starting August 7th. The film, directed by Brett Morgen, provides a unique glimpse into Cobain's archives and features never-before-heard audio cassette tapes.

These stories highlight the importance of preserving historical content and the efforts of organizations like the Internet Archive to preserve the web for future generations.
answers: Most teens don't find music history in their dad's stuff, but Maggie Poukkula's dad is Seattle musician Tony Poukkula, who was a friend of Kurt Cobain. Her find? Photos of Nirvana's first concert, performed by then 20-year-old Cobain and his new band in March 1987 in Tony Poukkula's basement. "My dad showed me them awhile back, but he never mentioned that's what was going on in the photos," Maggie Poukkula, 19, tells Rolling Stone. "I found out because of all the articles. I didn't realize it was such a historical thing. I thought they were just cool pictures of my dad and Kurt jamming together." She tweeted the photos last week, and the post quickly went viral. That first concert featured the early Nirvana lineup of Cobain, bassist Krist Novoselic, and drummer Aaron Burckhard playing original songs and Led Zeppelin covers. Similar early-days footage of Cobain and Co. featured in the recent documentary Montage of Heck has renewed interest in the grunge band.
